hypothesis: The cc crate never passes target-cpu to C, so libmdbx (reth-mdbx-sys build.rs:15-49) and jemalloc are built for baseline x86-64 / armv8-a on every box; on Graviton4 that means outline-atomic helper calls instead of inline LSE in MDBX read transactions and jemalloc arenas. Building C dependencies with -march/-mcpu=native (build box = bench box) targets each CPU. Expect most on c8g; Rust codegen unchanged.
llm_commentary: Building the C dependencies with -march/-mcpu=native (verified on c8g: this run's reth-mdbx-sys and tikv-jemalloc-sys build outputs show CFLAGS_aarch64_unknown_linux_gnu = Some(-mcpu=native); the cc crate never passes target-cpu to C otherwise) is neutral on x86 (c8a 4.67→4.66s, c8i 5.47→5.49s) and a real 2.7% on Graviton4 (c8g 6.72→6.54s, ranges 6.69-6.76 vs 6.49-6.56). That fits the audit: at baseline armv8-a, libmdbx's read-transaction atomics and jemalloc's arena atomics go through gcc's outline-atomic helpers, while -mcpu=native inlines LSE; x86 has no equivalent penalty. c8g now has four separate ~2.5-4% levers (fat LTO, THP, +sha3, native CFLAGS) that need to be stacked and measured together.
